title: Comparison square from subset Cech coordinates to injective coefficient terms
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, $V=\bigcup_iD(f_i)$ and $D_S=D(\prod_{j\in S}f_j)$. Let $J$ be an arbitrary unbounded K-injective cochain complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let $K,T$ be complexes of $A$-modules, with degreewise $A$-linear isomorphisms $\sigma_n:K^n\cong\Gamma(V,J^n)$ and $\tau_n:T^n\cong\prod_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(r)}\Gamma(D_S,J^{n+1-|S|})$. Assume $\sigma$ identifies the differential of $K$ with the sectionwise differential of $J$, and $\tau$ identifies the differential of $T$ with the signed total formula: at $S$ its vertical term is $(-1)^{|S|-1}d_J$ and its horizontal term is the sum over $j\in S$ of restriction from $D_{S\setminus\{j\}}$, multiplied by $(-1)^{|\{i\in S:i<j\}|}$, with empty deletions zero. All coefficient degrees are transported by their displayed integer equalities. Let $\alpha:K\to T$ be a chain map which under these coordinates is restriction from $V$ on singleton coordinates and zero on all larger subsets. The open inclusion inequalities and degree equalities in the Lean signature specify only the transports in these formulas. There exist a complex $I$ of module sheaves with every $I^n$ injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], complexes $K_1,T_1$ of $A$-modules, degree isomorphisms $\sigma_1,\tau_1$, and an augmentation $\alpha_1:K_1\to T_1$ satisfying the very same section, signed subset-total and singleton augmentation formulas with $I$ in place of $J$. There also exist chain maps $a:K\to K_1$ and $b:T\to T_1$ such that $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\alpha b=a\alpha_1$. No assertion about the homology of either augmentation is part of this conclusion.

proof.text: Install SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian for the structure sheaf and use the existing functorial kInjectiveResolutionFunctor and toKInjectiveResolution. The resolution map g is a quasi-isomorphism, its target I is K-injective and its terms are injective. By CochainComplex.IsKInjective.quasiIso_iff obtain a homotopy equivalence with hom=g.

Define the additive section-evaluation functor E on V using modulesSpecToSheaf and set K₁ to E applied degreewise to I. The supplied σ and section differential equation give a chain isomorphism c:K ≅ E(J) using HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents. Define a=c.hom ≫ E(g). Functor.mapHomotopyEquiv applies E to the inverse and homotopies; its quasiIso_hom proves E(g) is a quasi-isomorphism. Compose with the chain isomorphism to prove QuasiIso a. The identity coordinates σ₁ and the construction of a give the section and comparison-coordinate equations by reflexivity.

Apply the arbitrary-coefficient coordinate construction to J,I,g,T,τ and the explicitly constructed K₁,σ₁. It supplies T₁,τ₁,α₁,b, the signed total differential and singleton augmentation equations, and the component formula for b. Prove the augmentation square in Lean: cancel τ₁ degreewise and evaluate each subset. On a singleton, substitute the coordinate formulas and the section comparison equation for a. The naturality square of g and restriction commutes after transport of coefficient degrees, proved by equality induction. On a larger subset both singleton augmentations vanish and g sends zero to zero. Combine the constructed witnesses, this square, the injectivity of the terms of I, the section equation for K₁ and the proved QuasiIso a.
